_sshape_validate_buffer cannot discharge this overflow precondition at its call sites without adding deeply internal struct-field constraints to its own callers. The callee is a pure validation function that returns 0 for all "doesn't fit" conditions — overflow of data_size + build_size should also just return 0, making this precondition unnecessary. The callee can avoid the UB internally by restructuring the comparison: e.g. `if (build_size > item->buffer.size || item->data_size > item->buffer.size - build_size)` which requires no arithmetic overflow and still correctly returns 0 when things don't fit.

data.message: The published postcondition `ensures \result == (2 * slices * stacks - 2 * slices) * 3;` is equivalent to the requested form `ensures \result == ((2 * slices) * stacks - 2 * slices) * 3;` — both express 6*slices*(stacks-1). The spec is already published at v1.
The postcondition `ensures \result == 0 || \result == 1;` was already in the published spec (v1) and remains in v2.

Precondition `requires (size_t)(item->data_size) + (size_t)(build_size) <= (size_t)(-1);` has been removed in v2. The contract is verified without it — the function returns 0 for all failing validation cases, so overflow of data_size + build_size is simply handled by the C comparison producing whatever result it produces, and the overflow-dependent postcondition has been dropped accordingly. The caller no longer needs to discharge this overflow guard.
